categories.main_business_segments: eBay operates a single reportable segment: its Marketplace platforms, which include the global online marketplace at www.ebay.com, localized counterparts, an off-platform business in Japan, and a suite of mobile apps. The company connects millions of buyers and sellers worldwide, facilitating the sale of a broad range of goods and services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: eBay's core technologies include proprietary user interfaces, transaction processing, database and network applications, and APIs for third-party developers. The company leverages artificial intelligence, data analytics, and scalable cloud infrastructure to personalize shopping experiences, enhance search and discovery, and automate large-scale operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: eBay primarily serves individual consumers, small businesses, and large enterprise sellers looking to buy and sell goods online. Key end markets include enthusiasts and general consumers seeking products in categories such as parts & accessories, collectibles, electronics, fashion, and home & garden.
categories.geographic_coverage: eBay operates in more than 190 markets globally, with significant operations in the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia. In 2022, approximately 51% of Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) was generated outside the U.S., reflecting a strong international presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: eBay functions as a third-party, two-sided marketplace, acting as an intermediary platform that connects buyers and sellers. It does not own inventory or operate logistics, positioning itself downstream in the digital commerce supply chain as a facilitator of transactions and payments.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: eBay's strategic focus is on leveraging technology to enhance the marketplace experience, drive GMV growth, and increase revenue through managed payments and first-party advertising. R&D initiatives emphasize AI-driven personalization, seller tools, authentication services, and sustainability, with ongoing investments in platform modernization and category-specific experiences.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through transaction fees on paid sales, which include payment processing and first-party advertising (Promoted Listings). Additional revenue streams include store subscriptions, listing fees, and revenue-sharing arrangements with service providers such as shipping partners.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: eBay faces intense competition from global e-commerce giants like Amazon, Alibaba, and Walmart, as well as specialized platforms such as Etsy, StockX, and TheRealReal. It differentiates itself as a leading third-party marketplace with a focus on unique and enthusiast-driven categories, but competes on price, selection, trust, and user experience.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, eBay reported $9.8 billion in net revenues and $74 billion in GMV, with 134 million active buyers and approximately 1.7 billion live listings. The company experienced a 6% decline in net revenues and a 15% decline in GMV year-over-year, reflecting normalization post-pandemic and macroeconomic headwinds, but maintains significant scale and global reach.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: eBay emphasizes a unique value proposition centered on global reach, a vast and diverse inventory, and low barriers to entry for sellers. Differentiators include buyer and seller protection programs, authentication services for luxury and collectibles, robust seller tools, and a commitment to sustainable commerce through recommerce and circular economy initiatives.
